title: One Job for Each Drawer
story: The repair bench at the youth club had become a jumble of cables, screws, and unnamed chargers. Jamal offered to sort it before the Saturday clinic, when neighbours brought radios and lamps. He grouped items that did the same job, then printed plain labels, because handwriting had smeared there before. Each drawer received one job, from power leads to fuses and tools that had to stay in the room. He tied a tag to every charger naming the device it fit. During the clinic a helper found a fuse in seconds instead of tipping the box onto the bench. A visitor started to pocket a spare lead, and the words on the drawer gave Jamal a polite reason to stop her. Afterwards he photographed the drawers so a later volunteer could restore the same order. The system was plain, yet the hour went to repairs rather than to searching.
